summary: The team is pivoting global marketing priority to China-based programs — Asia Star and the new Intelligent China — while closing out the knowledge website redesign and firefighting an Outlook lockout that's blocking the team this week.
summaryDetail: The dominant strategic thread is the June 30 global marketing sync decision to put Asia Star and Intelligent China first for search and AI visibility, demoting the US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) to a secondary tier, with Berkeley a possible third priority and all US programs folded into the audit phase. That decision now needs to convert into execution: Joseph's target-areas/prompts and audience-focus document is the gating item, alongside profiling existing Asia Star participants and CRM leads and launching the Intelligent China webpage to drive traffic. On the knowledge website redesign, the team has settled on keeping the current layout and two-menu structure with menu categorization improvements, dropping the standalone videos section in favor of topic-based dispersion and bringing BCI/BSI indices into the knowledge section; Joseph still owes the HTML file and a 30-minute feedback session is pending before Joker makes the design changes. This week's urgent distraction is an Outlook account lockout caused by stale saved passwords across devices — the team must re-login, clean up unused accounts, and confirm the backend unlock with CKGSB IT. Looking ahead, the Google Ads conversion-tracking audit brief is outstanding, and the October-dated items — the ESG report draft handoff, the Nov 13 EuroCham Shanghai event, the Yili digitalization enquiry, and Ira's homepage/knowledge PPT review — are queuing up behind the AACSB 2027 Global Impact Award submission already filed.
